title: Beacon merchant trial activation brief
content:
Executive summary:

Objective: run a 30-day merchant-facing POC with Beacon Retail to validate a conversational product discovery flow powered by Redwood Inference. The goal is to demonstrate sub-150ms median token latency on catalog search prompts, keep token cost under $0.0009 per user query on average, and prove observable quality improvement over the existing keyword search baseline for top-20 SKUs.

Why this POC: Beacon has a high-velocity, curated catalog and a downstream cadence of high-intent shoppers. They need a low-latency reranker + generative assistant to surface product options and concise reasons for recommendation while keeping throughput predictable during sale spikes. This POC tests Redwood’s model routing + caching + fallback patterns in a production-adjacent workload.

Success goals (SMART):
- Latency: median end-to-end response < 150ms for generation of short product snippets (<= 60 tokens) for 95% of traffic during a 10k QPS simulated load window.
- Cost: mean token spend per query <= $0.0009 under the configured batching and cache profile.
- Quality: 10% relative improvement in click-through-rate (CTR) on recommended SKUs vs the baseline in A/B basket lift tests with at least 1,200 impressions per variant.
- Reliability: 99.5% successful responses (no fallback content) during business-hours traffic in the pilot window.
- Security/compliance: no PII leaves Beacon’s VPC (proof via audit log samples and KMS usage).

Acceptance criteria (concrete tests):
1) Performance acceptance test:
   - Run a controlled load with the traffic mix generator (script: load-sim/beacon-queries-v2).
   - Measure median token latency and p95 against the SLO.
   - Pass if median <150ms and p95 <450ms for the primary route.

2) Cost evaluation:
   - Use Redwood Console cost breakdown for trial window and model variants.
   - Verify recorded average token cost <= $0.0009 per query after batching is enabled.

3) Quality evaluation:
   - Instrument UI to send impressions and clicks to a test bucket.
   - Run a 2-week A/B with canary traffic 50/50; compute CTR lift for top-20 SKUs.
   - Qualitative audit: product team samples 100 generated snippets and rates relevance >= 3/5 average.

4) Data handling and privacy:
   - Ensure access logs show KMS-wrapped keys for inference payloads (sample of 100 logs).
   - Confirm no customer PII is present in stored prompts or cached prefixes.

5) Operability:
   - On-call runbook verified with a simulated failure (GPU OOM) showing automated fallback to smaller model and alerting within 90s.

Proposed deployment approach (minimal risk path):
- Start Hosted API with a dedicated model route and prefix caching enabled.
- Configure autoscaling with a soft cap to emulate Dedicated throughput; enable burst policy for sale-window tests.
- After 7 days of stable telemetry and passing baseline acceptance tests, run a dry switch to Dedicated-reserved pool for a 72-hour stress window to validate predictable throughput.
- If Beacon must keep traffic inside their network, the private deployment option is documented as plan-B (requires VPC peering + HSM integration, estimated lead time 6–8 weeks).

Architecture notes (integration points):
- Beacon frontend -> Redwood API route /v1/generate-product-snippet (auth via Beacon JWT + Redwood API key mapper).
- Redwood route policy: prefer lowest-cost compatible model (q8_compat) with automatic fallback to q4f for short sequences.
- Caching: per-product prefix cache keyed by product-id+user-locale; TTL 30m.
- Observability hooks: tracing header (x-redwood-trace) to correlate ui request -> model request -> response.

Workshop plan (90-min kickoff):
- 0-10m: Introductions, success metrics alignment (owner: Asha).
- 10-25m: Architecture walkthrough and integration checklist (owner: Markus).
- 25-45m: Data and privacy constraints (owner: Priya).
- 45-65m: Acceptance tests, traffic shaping, and load script review (owner: Diego).
- 65-80m: Rollout and rollback strategies, SLO definitions (owner: Janelle).
- 80-90m: Next actions, immediate blockers, and assignment of owners.

Breakout tasks (post-workshop day 1):
- Beacon: export sample catalog subset (top 5k SKUs) and schema mapping (due +2 days).
- SE: provision trial route, initial model profile, and generate sample prompts (due +3 days).
- Infra: create test KMS key and logging sink (due +4 days).
- QA: prepare synthetic load script and baseline keyword search harness (due +5 days).

Roles & responsibilities (quick):
- Beacon product: dataset curation, UI A/B instrumentation, acceptance sign-off.
- Redwood SE: POC architecture, model routing config, troubleshooting, and runbook delivery.
- Redwood Infra: Dedicated pool setup, KMS/HSM proofs, and private deploy constraints.
- QA: synthetic load generation and CTR analysis.

Timeline & milestones (30-day):
- Day 0: Kickoff workshop.
- Day 1-5: Data handoff, SE provisioning, and internal smoke tests.
- Day 6-12: Performance tuning (batching, cache TTL, kernel hints).
- Day 13-20: A/B experiments and quality sampling.
- Day 21-26: High-load dedicated validation.
- Day 27-30: Final acceptance review and go/no-go decision.

Risk register (top 6):
- Risk: Traffic spike causes P95 to exceed SLO. Mitigation: pre-warm Dedicated burst and enable immediate fallback route to lighter quantized model.
- Risk: Sampled prompts contain customer emails. Mitigation: add prompt scrubbing lambda at ingestion and block-write to cache.
- Risk: Cost overruns during stress test. Mitigation: enable cost-controlled routing policy and hourly budget alerts.
- Risk: SDK incompatibility in Beacon mobile. Mitigation: fall back to server-side call and test both clients in QA.
- Risk: Rollout downtime during switch to Dedicated. Mitigation: blue-green plan with traffic splitting and progressive ramp.
- Risk: Compliance team needs proof of dataset lineage. Mitigation: collect transfer log artifacts and provide hashed samples.

Early signals of success (KPIs to watch first 7 days):
- Median generation latency under 150ms on production-like load.
- Cache hit rate > 22% for repeat product impressions.
- Avg token cost aligns with target within 10% margin.
- Qualitative >70% of sampled snippets rated relevant by product SMEs.

Post-POC decision matrix (recommended gating):
- Pass: all SLOs met + CTR lift >= 8% -> propose Reserved Dedicated contract and feature rollout plan.
- Conditional pass: performance SLOs met, quality below target -> 30-day remediation plan (relabel data, prompt engineering).
- Fail: latency or reliability SLO breaches or data policy violations -> stop and switch to private deployment feasibility study.

Immediate next actions (owners):
- Asha: schedule kickoff and send invite with pre-reads (today).
- Beacon: export sample catalog slice and share data access (in 48h).
- SE (Diego): provision trial route and share model profile JSON (in 72h).
- Infra (Markus): create KMS test key and confirm logging sink (in 96h).

Notes & open questions (work-in-progress):
- Need clarification from Beacon on whether user-level personalization is in-scope for the trial (affects caching and privacy).
- Confirm expected peak concurrent users during merchant sales events (Beacon to provide telemetry).
- Decide whether to include a short-text reranker chain or a single-pass generator for the first 14 days.

Appendix: quick test prompts (for QA):
- "Find sustainable running shoes under $120 for trail running"
- "Best earbuds for noise cancellation and long battery life under $200"
- "Lightweight waterproof jacket for rainy climate, female, size M"

Contact: Asha Raman (asha@redwood.ai) — SE lead for Beacon merchant trial.
